recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Revisit only if a new work-group decision changes Bundle.type collection processing semantics or requires additional normative constraints beyond the existing definition.
issue_request: FHIR-16389 was a Published FHIR-core change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking that Bundle.type = collection be better defined for normative use or removed from normative content. The approved resolution was to define Collection as a set of resources collected into a single package for ease of distribution with no processing obligations or behavioral rules beyond persistence.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by commit 73b59a01de7c0190de0e5a7f2c14a617aab25af7, 'GF#16389 - fix bundle definition', which inserted the approved text into the historical Bundle spreadsheet source. Later source refactoring moved the definition into source/bundle/codesystem-bundle-type.xml.
additional_context: Bundle is active in source/fhir.ini, and the current Collection concept definition exactly matches the approved FHIR-16389 wording. FHIR-10754 earlier changed the concept from 'document' to 'package', and that correction is retained. FHIR-32015 later clarified operations-page guidance about response Bundle types without changing the collection code definition. Zulip and Confluence searches found no later work-group record contradicting the current source.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The authoritative current code system source already satisfies the issue, and the surrounding Bundle narrative is not misleading enough to justify duplicating or restating the same definition elsewhere.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Published issue changed the collection definition from document to package; the current FHIR-16389 wording retains that correction.
Later Published operations-page issue clarified that operation response Bundles are typically collection but can use other types; it does not conflict with the collection code definition.
